extracted.intended_audience: general news readers interested in media, satire, and social-media policy (Fox News audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A news report describing a social-media moderation action against a satire publisher and summarizing platform policies, fact-checker actions, and platform enforcement consequences. Focuses on how satire interacts with hate-speech rules and distribution/demonetization practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twitter hateful conduct policy (no harassment on protected characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: "You may not promote violence against, threaten, or harass other people on the basis of race, ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, religious affiliation, age, disability, or serious disease."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by Twitter to justify locking @TheBabylonBee; the policy prohibits harassment based on listed protected characteristics. In the article this policy is cited as the basis for action against content that targets a transgender individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted misgendering and deadnaming of transgender individuals treated as hateful conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter announced in 2018 that it would consider "targeted misgendering or dead naming of transgender individuals" to be a violation of its "hateful conduct" policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms consider deliberate misgendering or use of a prior name (deadnaming) of a transgender person to be abusive/hateful conduct. This specific application of the hateful-conduct policy was the rationale invoked for the Babylon Bee tweet suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement mechanics for locked accounts (delete violative tweet to regain access)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an account is locked for violating the hateful conduct policy, the account owner is required to delete the violative Tweet before regaining access; the account may be restored after deletion (the article cites a 12-hour restoration countdown that won't begin until deletion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical enforcement procedure: temporary lock, demand deletion of specific content, then timed restoration. This affects how publishers respond (e.g., choosing not to delete as a stance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facebook 'satire exception' guidance — "true satire does not 'punch down'"
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook updated its "satire exception" to the Hate Speech Community Standard, warning that "true satire does not ‘punch down.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms may distinguish satire from hate speech, but will consider whether satire targets vulnerable groups (punching down). Violating satire exception guidance can lead to demonetization or distribution penalties; the article cites Facebook warning and later demonetization of the Babylon Bee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checker evaluation of satire vs misinformation (unclear/muddy satire may be labeled false)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-checkers like Snopes have evaluated Babylon Bee pieces and questioned whether "fanning the flames of controversy and muddying the details of a news story" qualifies as satire, at times labeling pieces "false."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a satirical piece blurs facts or could be mistaken for real news, fact-checkers may treat it as misinformation rather than satire; such labels can trigger platform actions (reduced distribution) and reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform consequences for repeat offenders and for content deemed to incite or mislead (throttling, demonetization, reduced distribution, deplatforming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms may throttle reach, demonetize, reduce distribution for "repeat offenders," demonetize content they claim incites violence, and in some cases lock accounts or take further action (demonetization, distribution penalties, temporary suspensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article: Facebook warned The Babylon Bee that "repeat offenders will see their distribution reduced," Facebook demonetized the Bee for a piece it claimed constituted incitement to violence, Twitter locked the account and required deletion. These are practical enforcement levers platforms use against publishers they judge to violate policies.
